text:
marta: heads-up, ran into a weird HF->Redwood chat_template conversion bug that only shows up after quantizing to 4-bit. seems like empty choice blocks are getting collapsed and an 'assistant:' prefix is leaking into the rendered prompt. breaking a bunch of evals :confused:

nina: :eyes: can you paste a minimal repro? is this on the jinja chat_template or the pre-rendered messages?

marta: it's in the jinja chat_template. minimal snippet below. works on HF runtime but after our conversion flow -> tokenization -> quant run we get truncated options and an extra 'assistant:' at the start of the assistant message body.

marta: ```jinja
{% for opt in choices %}
- {{ opt.text }}
{% else %}
- (no options provided)
{% endfor %}

{{ user_message }}
```

ryan: model name + tokenizer? might be special tokens mapping issue (assistant/system role tokens).

marta: model: huggingface.co/opensource/fast-chat-x, tokenizer: hf-tokenizer v0.12 with added <|assistant|> and <|system|> tokens in config.json. conversion step maps hf roles -> redwood roles, but I suspect the jinja pre-renderer and our sentinel inserter disagree on whether to include the assistant sentinel inline or as a separate role prefix.

sam: two possibilities: 1) empty Jinja 'else' block renders a single dash + newline which our prompt-trimmer strips when running the prefix sanitizer; 2) our conversion inserts a role sentinel after rendering but before tokenization and the quant tokenizer's byte-split merges sentinel into next token leading to 'assistant:' token appearing in-stream.

sam: quick grep i ran:```bash
# suspect: config.json role tokens ordering
jq '.model_special_tokens' config.json
# or check tokenizer added tokens list
python -c "from tokenizers import Tokenizer;print(Tokenizer.from_file('tokenizer.json').get_vocab_size())"
```

nina: eval-bot posted the CI dump: deploy-bot caught a prompt-diff for the policy tests. eval-bot shows a -7% pass rate on the conditional-choice tests after quantization (4-bit), but float32 baseline is fine.

eval-bot: metric summary: conditional-choice-suite: baseline acc 0.92 -> quant4 acc 0.85; avg token-shift 2.1 tokens earlier; observed extra token '\"assistant:\"' prepended in 18/200 cases. diffs: link to CI artifact: https://ci.internal/runs/3829/artifacts/prompt-diffs.txt

ryan: interesting. can you attach the raw token ids (pre and post quant decoding) for one failing case? that will tell if tokenization fused the sentinel.

marta: attached below (trimmed):
```
# before quant (ids): 1245 98 0 4012 77 9001 333
# after quant-run decode: "assistant: - Option A
- Option B
User: what's next?"
```

sam: that confirms two things: the sentinel token is being decoded as literal text in the quant pathway. likely our tokenizer merges the sentinel into a subword token because of byte-level bpe differences in the quantized runtime. we saw similar with other added tokens when quant table packing changed split points.

marta: workaround that fixed our local evals: explicitly render choice blocks to plaintext before handing to the conversion pipeline (i.e., pre-render jinja choices -> pass as single assistant message string), and add a small sanitizer step to escape any leading 'assistant:' literal in assistant messages. breaks the templating purity but unblocks gating tests.

ryan: long-term fix: ensure the conversion pipeline normalizes special tokens to dedicated token ids BEFORE any quant-specific tokenizer step. probably need a small patch in our hf->redwood mapping to always add sentinel tokens to tokenizer.vocab (and commit tokenizer.json) and add unit tests for byte-split stability under quantization.

sam: filing ticket RW-1342 with repro, sample token ids, and suggested patch (normalize special tokens earlier). I'll also add a tiny integration test to the quant CI that runs token-split consistency using our quant tokenizer shim.

marta: created PR draft with the pre-render sanitizer as emergency patch (wip): https://git.internal/rw/pr/1209 - adds test + comment explaining why we need it. cc @ryan for review.

deploy-bot: CI failed on pr/1209: prompt-regression-suite timeout 1/40 tests; rerun queued.

nina: ok plan sounds good. after RW-1342 lands we should remove emergency sanitizer and add a conversion-mode flag so private deployments can opt-in to legacy behavior if needed. also add an eval alert for sudden token shifts >1.5 tokens for any prompt family.

marta: thanks all — i'll attach the full failing artifact and ping team when PRs are green. :thumbsup:
